boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along Bristol’s Hope, High, Court, Wood, and Thames Street corridors, each with a documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Pick up Bristol context
cards.subtitle: Hope Street corridor — 400 Hope Street
cards.notes: Begin at the building that houses the Bristol Visitor Center, then use its maps and brochures to choose a focused walk through downtown.
cards.short_summary: A historic Hope Street hall that serves as Bristol’s visitor-center stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Burnside Memorial Hall at 400 Hope Street houses the Bristol Visitor Center and is the starting point for Explore Bristol’s downtown walking tour.
cards.access_notes: The Bristol Visitor Center is seasonal; confirm hours before making a special trip.

cards.title: Settle in with local collections
cards.subtitle: Hope Street corridor — 525 Hope Street
cards.notes: Bring a reading or research task and use the library’s public setting; check the posted day-specific hours before you head downtown.
cards.short_summary: A public library on Hope Street with weekday evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Rogers Free Library is at 525 Hope Street and lists Monday–Thursday hours of 9 a.m.–8 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–8 p.m.; Friday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Sunday.

cards.title: See an 1810 Federal mansion
cards.subtitle: Hope Street corridor — 500 Hope Street
cards.notes: Pause outside to document the Federal-style mansion, or consult the house museum’s current tour information before planning an interior visit.
cards.short_summary: A documented 1810 mansion on Bristol’s central Hope Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Linden Place at 500 Hope Street is a Federal-style mansion built in 1810 for George and Charlotte DeWolf.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is distinct from house-museum tours; check the museum directly for visit availability.

cards.title: Find the gallery behind Linden Place
cards.subtitle: Wardwell Street corridor — 10 Wardwell Street
cards.notes: Walk one block off Hope Street to the main galleries behind Linden Place, and check the museum’s current exhibition details before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit art museum with main galleries on Wardwell Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Bristol Art Museum’s main galleries are at 10 Wardwell Street, behind the Linden Place museum.
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s own site for current gallery hours and exhibition access.

cards.title: Trace Rhode Island’s rotating legislature
cards.subtitle: High Street corridor — 240 High Street
cards.notes: Circle the Town Common to view the 1819 statehouse, then watch for a Bristol Statehouse Foundation open-house opportunity for interior access.
cards.short_summary: A High Street landmark that once hosted Rhode Island’s legislature.
cards.evidence_claim: Built in 1819, the Bristol State House was one of five Rhode Island statehouses and hosted the rotating legislature into the 1850s.
cards.source_title: Bristol State House | Explore Bristol RI
cards.access_notes: Interior visits are tied to open-house events; verify an event before expecting access.

cards.title: Follow Bristol’s plaque trail
cards.subtitle: Court Street corridor — 48 Court Street
cards.notes: Use the Society’s museum and local-history resources to add context to the downtown streetscape; verify open days before arriving for research.
cards.short_summary: A former jail building housing Bristol history collections and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bristol Historical & Preservation Society is in the former Bristol County Jail at 48 Court Street and holds museum exhibits on Bristol history.
cards.access_notes: Explore Bristol lists Society openings on Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday afternoons; verify before visiting.

cards.title: Read Bristol’s Azores connection
cards.subtitle: Wood Street corridor — corner of Wood and Franklin streets
cards.notes: Stop at the corner park’s benches and mosaic-focused setting, then read the site as a marker of Bristol’s connection with Lagoa, São Miguel.
cards.short_summary: A small Wood Street corner park representing Bristol’s link to its Azorean sister city.
cards.evidence_claim: Mosaico Park sits at Wood and Franklin streets and was designed as a symbol of Bristol’s connection with Lagoa, São Miguel, Azores.
cards.access_notes: A town park; observe posted park rules and closure times.

cards.title: Walk native plantings by Silver Creek
cards.subtitle: Hope Street corridor — 799 Hope Street
cards.notes: Take the winding paths through this passive park and pause at a bench or overlook for birdwatching, sketching, or a quiet photo break.
cards.short_summary: A Hope Street naturalistic park with trails, plantings, and scenic overlooks.
cards.evidence_claim: Thomas Park at Silver Creek is a 5.1-acre Hope Street park with native plantings, walking paths, benches, and scenic overlooks.
cards.access_notes: Town park rules apply; Bristol ordinances list town-park closure from sunset to 6 a.m. unless otherwise authorized.

cards.title: Document Bristol’s boatbuilding legacy
cards.subtitle: Hope Street corridor — One Burnside Street
cards.notes: Photograph the waterfront museum setting from public areas, or plan a museum visit to explore its Herreshoff and America’s Cup collections.
cards.short_summary: A maritime museum at the Hope and Burnside streets corner.
cards.evidence_claim: Herreshoff Marine Museum is at One Burnside Street, at the corner of Hope Street and Burnside Street in Bristol.
cards.access_notes: The museum posts seasonal hours and admission rates; review its visit page before planning indoor access.

cards.title: Finish at the bike-path terminus
cards.subtitle: Thames Street corridor — Bristol Harbor
cards.notes: End a downtown walk at this harbor park, where the East Bay Bike Path reaches Bristol; bring a bike or simply follow the waterfront edge.
cards.short_summary: The Bristol Harbor endpoint of the East Bay Bike Path.
cards.evidence_claim: The East Bay Bike Path reaches its terminus at Independence Park at Bristol Harbor, at the entrance to the Bristol Waterfront Historic District.
cards.source_title: East Bay Bike Path (1987) | Rhode Island State Parks
cards.access_notes: The East Bay Bike Path is open year-round from sunrise to sunset; town park closure rules apply at Independence Park.
